source: General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — Sweet Corn Production Handbook (ផលិតកម្មដំណំពោតផ្អែម), in partnership with SNV
text:
A mature corn plant's parts include the root system, stem, leaves, tassel (male flower), silk/ear with husk (female flower and grain-bearing structure), and roots. The document illustrates two root-system types observed in corn: plants with a fibrous/compact root system, and plants with a spread-out (loose) root system.

The document also distinguishes corn by ear type, showing images of: fresh sweet corn (ពោតផ្អែម), roasted corn (ពោតអាំង), boiled corn (ពោតស្ងោរ), and corn husks (សំបកពោត / the ear wrapped in husk with silk visible).

For cross-pollination biology: the tassel (ចង្អុរ/ថង់ផ្កា, male flower) and silk (ចង្កា/ស្រៅ, female flower) are shown in a diagram of corn's reproductive development, illustrating how pollination between the male and female flower parts leads to kernel formation on the ear.
